output.summary: A genus of evergreen shrubs and trees, mostly native to Australia, with a few occurring naturally in Malesia, seven native only to New Caledonia and one to Lord Howe Island. Many have peeling papery bark or aromatic, oil-dotted leaves, while flowers are grouped into bottlebrush-like heads or spikes.
output.edibilityNote: M. cajuputi oil is used in Southeast Asia to add fragrance to food.
